items.title: Towards autonomous medical artificial intelligence agents
items.summary: A large language model artificial intelligence agent operating in a sandboxed electronic health record system can autonomously take patient histories, order tests, interpret findings, diagnose conditions and propose treatments, outperforming experienced clinicians while adhering to safety standards and clinical guidelines.

items.title: Spatial distribution of the proteome in the human body and in cancers
items.summary: A spatially resolved map of the human proteome across a variety of healthy tissues and cancers provides wide-ranging insights in developmental biology and oncology, and could aid the identification of therapeutic targets and development of treatments for cancer.

items.title: A 98-qubit trapped-ion quantum computer with all-to-all connectivity
items.summary: A new quantum computer, Quantinuum Helios, which is a 98-qubit trapped-ion quantum processor built on the QCCD architecture, demonstrates performance well beyond classical capabilities and provides a path for scaling up quantum computing.

items.title: Reconfigurable quantum computer juggles 98 qubits
items.summary: A quantum computer based on trapped ions can connect any two quantum bits, reaching performance levels that conventional computers cannot match.

items.title: Cell transplant across the tree of life hints at how animals emerged
items.summary: Embryonic ‘organizer cells’ can tell embryos of various phyla what kind of body to build.

items.title: A blastoporal organizer in a ctenophore
items.summary: Experiments using the comb jelly Mnemiopsis leidyi and the sea anemone Nematostella vectensis reveal that the emergence of a core signalling pathway may have been a key innovation enabling the transition to multicellularity in animals.

items.title: Lethal plague outbreaks in Lake Baikal hunter-gatherers 5,500 years ago
items.summary: Analyses of ancient DNA from hunter-gatherers near Lake Baikal in southeast Siberia around 5,500 years ago indicate that highly virulent Yersinia pestis emerged earlier than previously estimated, far from the next known cases of infection in Late Neolithic Europe.

items.title: DNA from hunter-gatherer teeth reveals secrets of ancient plague
items.summary: Analysis shows evidence of deadly outbreaks 5,500 years ago — plus, a prototype dark-matter detector.

items.title: Emergent decadal predictability in Antarctic contribution to sea-level rise
items.summary: Although Antarctic ice loss projections diverge widely by 2100, this Perspective shows that present-day rates robustly predict mid-century sea level rise, providing a firm basis for near-term planning, while highlighting priorities for model development aimed at resolving longer-term sea level rise uncertainty.

items.title: A mosaic of whole-body representations on the human precentral gyrus
items.summary: A comprehensive map of the human motor cortex at single-neuron resolution is described.

items.title: Mapping the neuronal building blocks of human language with language models
items.summary: Wide-scale recordings reveal neurons in the human brain that encode fundamental components of language such as the grammatical relationships between words, their parts of speech and the higher-order syntactic structure of phrases and sentences.

items.title: Reimagining machine vision with optical computing
items.summary: A general-purpose artificial-intelligence vision system for use in image-sensing devices has been developed by embedding fundamentals of core computer-vision operations into a light-manipulating planar material called an optical metasurface. A prototype enables accurate, real-time perception and processing across diverse tasks, suggesting that this could be a solution for rapid, low-energy, on-device vision intelligence.

items.title: How the brain builds sentences, neuron by neuron
items.summary: Neural maps reveal the specialized cells that produce speech.

items.title: The ancestors of eukaryotic cells contained a mix of genes from various microbes
items.summary: Reconstruction of the ancestral gene repertoire of eukaryotic cells reveals traces of a series of close, long-term interactions with diverse microorganisms, and a role of viruses in gene exchange. The findings challenge the view that eukaryotic cells evolved from a simple merger of just two organisms.

items.title: Analysis of 173,303 exomes and genomes in the Pakistan Genome Resource
items.summary: The Pakistan Genome Resource compiles biobank data from 173,303 individuals with high familial relatedness, broadening the catalogue of human genetic variation and establishing a population-specific genomic reference for Pakistan.

items.title: Rock weathering can counteract river CO<sub>2</sub> emissions induced by permafrost thaw
items.summary: Permafrost thaw on the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau increases rock-weathering rates while reducing river CO2 emissions, suggesting geological carbon fluxes may eventually outpace thaw-driven emissions.

items.title: Optical metasurfaces for general vision processing on the edge
items.summary: By embedding core computer vision principles into a large-scale optical metasurface, an efficient vision processing system using far fewer parameters is demonstrated to outperform many digital models and enables deployment on edge devices.

items.title: These ‘master’ proteins protect us from deadly mutations — and could inspire new drugs
items.summary: Biology has clever ways to mask the effects of potentially harmful gene mutations. Scientists are investigating how this ‘buffering’ works — and how to exploit it.

items.title: Structure of the pre-initiation complex explains CMGE biogenesis
items.summary: Cryo-electron microscopy and biochemical reconstitution experiments in yeast provide insight into the assembly of the CMGE complex, a helicase that establishes bidirectional DNA replication in eukaryotic cells, and elucidate the role of the firing factor Sld2.

items.title: Fast formation to reinforce lithium-rich cathodes
items.summary: Fast formation in lithium-ion batteries outperforms conventional slow formation, lowering costs and improving battery capacity, stability and cycle life, offering broader application to electrode systems.

items.title: Cortical development dynamics across autism spectrum disorder mouse models
items.summary: Using single-nucleus multi-omic sequencing, diverse autism spectrum disorder-linked gene mutations converge on transient, stage-specific disruptions in early brain development, and highlight sex-specific gene expression alterations.

items.title: Freezing brain damage in its tracks: cooling drugs limit stroke injury in mice
items.summary: A two-drug combination induces hypothermia in mice by lowering metabolism and dilating blood vessels.

items.title: Fiery data hint that controlled forest fires benefit human health
items.summary: Analysis of wildfire in California suggests a net reduction in exposure to blaze-related air pollution.

items.title: How the zebrafish brain weaves recent experiences into future decisions
items.summary: Animals often use recent experience to guide future choices. Whole-brain imaging in larval zebrafish (Danio rerio) reveals a dedicated neural circuit that governs history-biased decisions: the thalamus maintains the most recent event as a stable pattern of neuronal activity, and the brainstem integrates recent experiences into a continuous signal that biases future action.

items.title: Probing picometre-scale interlayer deformations via hyperbolic polaritons
items.summary: A new polaritonic optical method that uses the mid-infrared out-of-plane hyperbolic polaritons mode is described and experimentally validated to allow the examination of picometre-scale interlayer deformations, providing a bridge between nanomechanics and photonics.

items.title: A prototype differential atom interferometer for fundamental physics
authors: M. G. D. van der Grinten
M. G. D. van der Grinten
items.summary: A prototype differential atom interferometer operates at the standard quantum limit with no excess noise beyond atom shot noise, achieving performance in line with the specifications for future long-baseline atom interferometers.

items.title: Molecular basis of polyadenylated RNA fate determination in the nucleus
items.summary: Biochemical, structural and cell biological analyses reveal that UAP56 (DDX39B) assembles with a TREX-2–like module that redirects non-functional polyadenylated RNAs from export to degradation.

items.title: Confined migration induces non-lethal DNA damage in developing neurons
items.summary: The migration of neurons in developing cerebral and cerebellar cortices is accompanied by massive DNA double-strand breaks due to mechanostress during passage through narrow interstitial spaces.

items.title: Cucurbituril-based anion-conducting membranes with supramolecular nanopores
items.summary: A supramolecular strategy, in which uniform, dynamic nanopores are constructed, overcomes the limitations of limited structural control, mechanical fragility or demanding synthesis in nanoporous anion-conducting membranes, providing a versatile tool for molecularly engineering transport pathways.

items.title: Oceans in Asia smash heat records — what it means for extreme weather
items.summary: Report shows region is particularly vulnerable to the effects of climate change.

items.title: Navigating a crowded developing brain leaves neurons with broken DNA
items.summary: As neurons migrate to their final destinations in the forming brain, their DNA gets damaged. The brain has evolved a fix, but there can be lasting consequences if repair fails.

items.title: Revealing competitive interfacial reactions in high-energy Li–S batteries
items.summary: Visualization of concentration-driven phase segregation within high-concentration interfacial layers in the context of high-energy lithium–sulfur batteries using liquid-cell electrochemical transmission electron microscopy reveals competitive interfacial reactions under lean electrolyte conditions at different phase boundaries.

items.title: CHPO coordinates chilling recovery and nitrogen use in rice
items.summary: A rice gene, CHPO, links chilling resilience with nitrogen-use efficiency, revealing a domestication-shaped regulatory mechanism that could guide breeding of climate-resilient, sustainable rice varieties.

items.title: Light-controlled microgripper punches above its weight
items.summary: A microscale gripper that can be opened and closed using light can fit into tight spaces and perform tasks linked to clinical applications.

items.title: El Niño in a thermally saturated world
items.summary: El Niño in a thermally saturated world

items.title: Brexit tore apart European science — now the research rifts are healing
items.summary: The UK’s share of EU research funding is climbing, but lost networks will be harder to recover.

items.title: The brain region that could provide a cognitive ‘reservoir’ in old age
items.summary: Having a greater tissue volume in some parts of the cerebellum is linked to higher scores on cognitive tests.

items.title: Optical fibre gripper for high-performance 3D micromanipulation
items.summary: A miniature three-dimensional optical fibre gripper enables powerful, precise micromanipulation of particles and single cells in confined spaces, bridging the gap between optical and mechanical tweezers.

items.title: Visualizing the impact of quenched disorder on 2D electron Wigner solids
items.summary: A technique combining atomically resolved scanning tunnelling microscopy with neural-quantum-state quantum Monte Carlo simulation of disordered 2D electron Wigner solids establishes a powerful framework to enable the clear identification of two distinct defect-induced disorder regimes.

items.title: The EU needs to back its ambition to end animal testing with cash
items.summary: The European Union has declared that it wants to stop using animals in chemical safety testing. Its goal will need a timeline and a serious funding commitment.

items.title: Clues to the sloth’s sloth found in its genome
items.summary: Sequencing shows duplication of genes that affect mitochondria, the organelles that provide energy for cells.

items.title: A distant brown dwarf coplanar to a warm Jupiter and a hot super-Earth
items.summary: Analysis of long-term radial velocity data and transit time variations, induced by a super-Earth, a warm Jupiter and a brown dwarf in a coplanar orbit around the relatively young star TOI201.

items.title: Should nicotine be regulated like a narcotic? A Pacific nation makes the case
items.summary: Existing global efforts to reduce harms caused by smoking have targeted tobacco smoking, but vapes containing nicotine are also harmful.

items.title: Mathematicians are developing rules for AI use — other fields should follow
items.summary: The mathematics community is right to call for transparency, integrity and fairness to be protected when AI tools are used. Researchers in other disciplines could learn from this approach.

items.summary: Towards Conversational AI for Disease Management

items.title: How do researchers choose what to work on?
items.summary: A scientist’s account of switching focus to tackle pressing problems, and researchers consider the best way to preserve eggs, in our weekly dip into Nature’s archive.
